session_note: The 194th General Court (2025-2026) is a two-year body; bills filed in 2025 remain the same live matter throughout 2026 without refiling, and joint committees routinely extend their own reporting deadlines by order (as H.4144 shows, extended from an earlier deadline to 2026-03-18). Formal sessions typically run into November 2026 with informal sessions after, and the biennium itself does not end until early January 2027, so a bill sitting in a House or Senate committee in mid-2026 is ordinarily still alive, not dead.

decisions.notes: Judgment call on bill_status_category: in Massachusetts practice, a committee sending a bill to 'accompany a study order' is the standard mechanism for disposing of a bill without a floor vote, and it does not proceed further under its own number this session -- matching the task guidance that a 'study order that effectively kills it' should be coded failed_died. The underlying subject (energy affordability/grid planning) is not dead as a policy matter (compare H.83 and HD.5404, still pending), but this specific bill number, H.4144, has reached a terminal disposition. Confidence reduced slightly (0.7) to reflect that this is an interpretive category assignment rather than an explicit 'rejected' vote.
